Resolves #992

Compensates `scrollTop` via `Neo.main.DomAccess.scrollTo` after `Neo.calendar.view.month.Component#onWheel` shifts the 6-week window downward (`value: data.scrollTop - removedHeight`, where `removedHeight` is measured from the actual rendered displacement `rects[1].top - rects[0].top` between the first removed week and the first retained week via `Neo.main.DomAccess.getBoundingClientRect`, falling back to `data.clientHeight - me.headerHeight` only when DOM rects are unavailable), and sets `overflow-anchor: none` on `.neo-c-m-scrollcontainer` so the engine owns the scroll seat identically across WebKit/Safari, Chromium, and Firefox without browser detection.

Evidence: L2 (Playwright real-browser WebKit 27.2 and branded Chromium e2e suite in `test/playwright/e2e/rendering/CalendarMonthRollover.spec.mjs` + L1 unit suite in `test/playwright/unit/calendar/MonthView.spec.mjs`) → L2 required (rendered scroll-anchor retention across uniform and tall 6-week rollovers in WebKit and Chromium).

## AC Evidence
No structured ACs on #992.
| Item | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Downward `onWheel` scroll compensation by actual rendered displacement | `src/calendar/view/month/Component.mjs:645-682` (`Neo.main.DomAccess.getBoundingClientRect({id: [weeks[0].id, weeks[6].id], windowId: me.windowId})` + `Neo.main.DomAccess.scrollTo({direction: 'top', id: me.vdom.cn[1].id, value: data.scrollTop - removedHeight, windowId: me.windowId})`) |
| Disable UA scroll anchoring on `.neo-c-m-scrollcontainer` | `resources/scss/src/calendar/view/month/Component.scss:13` (`overflow-anchor: none;`, matching `grid/Container.scss`, `grid/View.scss`, and `list/Buffered.scss`) |
| Real-browser regression coverage (WebKit 27.2 + Chromium across uniform and tall weeks) | Committed spec `test/playwright/e2e/rendering/CalendarMonthRollover.spec.mjs` (`2/2` passing on `head` across `webkit` and `chromium`, asserting `removedHeight > assumedHeight + 10` on tall July 14 week and `Math.abs(anchorDelta) < 5` across 3 consecutive rollovers); `base` vs `head` comparison receipt captured locally prior to `81ac97e4a6` and recorded in `## Test Evidence` below |
| Unit test coverage for downward and upward boundary scroll | `test/playwright/unit/calendar/MonthView.spec.mjs:140-245` (`3/3` passing) |

## Deltas from ticket
- Used `overflow-anchor: none` on `.neo-c-m-scrollcontainer` (matching `grid/Container.scss`, `grid/View.scss`, and `list/Buffered.scss`) plus actual rendered displacement (`rects[1].top - rects[0].top` between `weeks[0]` and `weeks[6]`) rather than adding browser detection to the `Neo` namespace or assuming a uniform `clientHeight - headerHeight` block height when a week row expands for extra events.
- `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; baseline `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/calendar/MonthView.spec.mjs` (`3/3` passed) and `npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs e2e/rendering/CalendarMonthRollover.spec.mjs` (`2/2` passed on committed `head` across WebKit 27.2 and Chromium; `4/4` with local `base` vs `head` control harness) ran.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** contained — a local calendar scroll-compensation repair using the existing DOM API and stylesheet, with no new public API or architectural abstraction.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** At `c509a1f91bb71ff922a39a6d2f010edb6e6910a6`, the source adds the missing explicit downward command, but its fixed-height assumption regresses the rendered date anchor. I exercised the actual `examples/calendar/basic` month view in Playwright WebKit 27.2 and branded Chromium, with the normal event fixture and a 1280×720 viewport. After setting the scroller to 1136, a real `mouse.wheel(0, 1)` rolls six weeks. The first rollover removes 577.97 px and is aligned; the next removes **597.42 px** because the July 14 week is taller, while `clientHeight - headerHeight` is **578**. The head therefore moves the preserved September 15 week anchor by **−20.42 px** in both browsers. With the same harness/data and only the changed module and CSS restored to their parent versions, that anchor moves **−1.42 px in WebKit / −0.42 px in Chromium**. `overflow-anchor: none` removes the browser's actual-height correction while the new command substitutes a nominal height. Current-head CI is green, but the added unit test stubs `scrollTo` and supplies uniform dimensions, so it cannot catch this. No generic browser-identification layer is needed.

**Findings:**

- [ ] **RA-1:** Correct downward rollover compensation so a preserved date row retains its rendered viewport offset when one or more removed weeks are taller than the nominal six-row allocation; use the actual rendered displacement or an equivalent stable-anchor mechanism rather than assuming `clientHeight - headerHeight` is the removed height. Add a real-browser regression with the existing calendar event fixture (or a deterministic tall-week fixture), covering consecutive downward rollovers in WebKit and Chromium with a base/control witness. Update the PR's L1-only sufficiency and no-post-merge-validation claims to the browser evidence actually obtained. This is a repair of the existing scroll outcome, not a request for browser detection or a new subsystem.

Reproduction: open `/examples/calendar/basic/index.html`, choose **Month** (default date July 21, 2024), use viewport 1280×720; for each of three consecutive iterations set `.neo-c-m-scrollcontainer.scrollTop` to `2 * (clientHeight - headerHeight) - 20`, retain a visible `.neo-week` id and its top offset, then send `page.mouse.wheel(0, 1)` and wait for the week-window replacement and presentation. The second iteration is the nonuniform-height witness; the first and third are controls. The controlled head fails in both engines; parent module/CSS controls retain the anchor. This is rendered headless-browser evidence, not an installed Safari-app claim.
